title: Linear independence of twisted invariant matrices survives scalar extension
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $S=K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, $n\in\mathbf N$, and $b:\operatorname{Gal}(S/K)\to\operatorname{GL}_n(S)$ any function. Let $A_b$ be [def-sc-matrix-descent-invariants], let $I$ be any index type and let $v:I\to A_b$ be $K$-linearly independent. Then the underlying matrices $(v_i)_{i\in I}$ are $S$-linearly independent in $\operatorname{Mat}_n(S)$. No local constancy or action laws for $b$ are assumed.

source.place: Tag 03R6 (Galois forms of matrix algebras); finite descent details expanded by an agent in lem-sc-matrix-descent-scalar-map-bijective step 4, coefficient uniqueness

proof.text: Embed the K-independent family into the matrix space by the injective subalgebra inclusion. Linear independence can be checked on finite subfamilies. Induct on a finite set of indices, starting from the empty set.

For the induction step, suppose v_i is in the S-span of the preceding independent vectors and choose coefficients c_j in their finite expansion. Applying M ↦ b(g)g(M)b(g)^(-1) to that equality gives another expansion with coefficients g(c_j). This uses only matrix distributivity, entrywise multiplicativity of g, scalar compatibility and the defining invariance of each v_j. Uniqueness of coefficients, by the inductive S-independence, gives g(c_j)=c_j for every g,j.

InfiniteGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed, with IsGalois K (SeparableClosure K), says each c_j is the image of a coefficient d_j in K. The resulting K-linear expansion of v_i contradicts K-linear independence, using linearIndepOn_insert. This completes finite-set induction and hence proves independence of the full family.
